Term 1 2025 – Cells and Microorganisms Test

Grade:   A    B    C    D    E Name:
Mark:  /62 marks

Description of assessment

This assessment is in three parts.

SECTION A – 20 multiple choice answer questions (20 marks).

SECTION B – 6 short answer questions (37 marks).

SECTION C – 1 extended response question (5 marks).

In your answers, remember:

  • Attempt all questions in the test.
  • To use appropriate biological terms and conventions.
  • To include details, reasons and examples where appropriate.

Assessment Conditions

You have the whole double (80 minutes) to complete this test if required.

Section A: Multiple Choice Questions — Choose ONE answer. Circle / click the letter. Each question is worth 1 mark.
Question 1:

Which of the following is not a statement outlined in the cell theory?

  • a. All living things are made up of cells
  • b. Cells come from pre-existing cells
  • c. Cells contain more than one chromosome
  • d. Cells are the structural and functional units of life
Question 2:

Which of the following lists the seven processes needed by living things?

  • a. Respiration, Movement, Growth, Reproduction, Digestion, Excretion and Synthesis
  • b. Photosynthesis, Circulation, Locomotion, Ingestion, Egestion, Secretion and Assimilation
  • c. Respiration, Circulation, Growth, Reproduction, Digestion, Excretion and Locomotion
  • d. Movement, Respiration, Sensitivity, Growth, Reproduction, Excretion and Nutrition
Question 3:

Which of the following cellular structures contains the genetic material of a eukaryotic cell?

  • a. Cytoplasm
  • b. Vacuole
  • c. Nucleus
  • d. Lysosome
Question 4:

A student has prepared a slide of plant cells and appropriately stained it. They then observe it with a light microscope using a ×10 eyepiece and a ×10 objective lens. At this magnification, which of the following details could be distinguished?

  • a. Nucleus, cell wall, mitochondria
  • b. Cell wall, mitochondria, ribosomes
  • c. Nucleus, cytoplasm, ribosomes
  • d. Nucleus, cytoplasm, cell wall
Question 5:

Why does some ER (endoplasmic reticulum) appear rough and others smooth?

  • a. Some ER have ribosomes attached.
  • b. Some waste products in the cell attach to the ER and make it look rough.
  • c. The ‘bumps’ on the ER are moving into the nucleus to be broken down.
  • d. Some ER hasn’t matured enough to have become rough.
Question 6:

A new species of organism is discovered. It possesses the characteristics listed below. Which one of these shows that it could NOT be classified as a bacterium?

  • a. Each cell is surrounded by a cell wall
  • b. It contains no chlorophyll
  • c. It has the ability to form spores
  • d. It has a small nucleus surrounded by a cell membrane
Question 7:

In general, organisms containing cells such as the one shown below…

  • a. Must digest nutrients before taking them into the cell
  • b. Synthesise their own organic materials from inorganic materials in the environment
  • c. Require complex organic molecules already synthesised by other organisms
  • d. Require no external energy source since they synthesise their own high energy compounds
Question 8:

As a result of mitosis in an animal cell, the daughter cells which are formed:

  • a. Have twice the number of chromosomes as the parent cells
  • b. Have half the number of chromosomes as the parent cells
  • c. Are genetically identical to the parent cells
  • d. Are genetically different from the parent cells
Question 9:

A structure found in plant cells, but NOT in animal cells is the:

  • a. Golgi body
  • b. Large central vacuole
  • c. Mitochondria
  • d. Cell membrane
Question 10:

The process of osmosis can occur in both living and non-living systems. The condition necessary for osmosis to occur is that:

  • a. Ions are transported from one solution to another
  • b. Large molecules are transported across a membrane
  • c. A membrane is permeable to water
  • d. Water moves from a low water concentration to a high-water concentration
Question 11:

Refer to the diagrams below, which show a process in which molecules move through a cell membrane.

The process shown in the diagram is:

  • a. Active transport
  • b. Diffusion
  • c. Osmosis
  • d. Facilitated diffusion
Question 12:

Which of the following statements is correct?

  • a. Photosynthesis is a process carried out by both autotrophs and heterotrophs
  • b. Photosynthesis and respiration both require oxygen
  • c. Respiration is a process only carried out by heterotrophs
  • d. Photosynthesis is a process which converts solar/light energy to chemical energy

Question 14:

The diagram below shows two beakers, each with a different concentration of sugar solution. The two beakers are separated by a semipermeable membrane. Use the diagram to answer the question below.

What would most likely happen in this situation above?

  • a. Water will move by osmosis from beaker A to beaker B
  • b. Water will move by osmosis from beaker B to beaker A
  • c. Sugar will move by osmosis from beaker A to beaker B
  • d. Sugar will move by osmosis from beaker B to beaker A
Question 15:

Refer to the diagram below which shows part of a specialised cell with some cellular structures.

Which of the following combinations correctly identifies structures X, Y and Z?

  • a. X = chloroplast, Y = Golgi body, Z = endoplasmic reticulum
  • b. X = mitochondria, Y = Golgi body, Z = endoplasmic reticulum
  • c. X = mitochondria, Y = endoplasmic reticulum, Z = Golgi body
  • d. X = chloroplast, Y = endoplasmic reticulum, Z = Golgi body
Question 16:

Refer to the diagram below, which shows the four stages of a cellular process.

The cellular process shown in the diagram is:

  • a. Binary fission in a prokaryotic cell
  • b. Binary fission in a eukaryotic cell
  • c. Mitosis in a prokaryotic cell
  • d. Mitosis in a eukaryotic cell
Question 17:

Which of the following statements correctly describes the function of the cell membrane?

  • a. The cell membrane strengthens the cell and gives it shape.
  • b. The cell membrane selectively permits materials to pass into and out of the cell.
  • c. The cell membrane contains a phospholipid bilayer embedded with proteins.
  • d. The cell membrane is composed of cellulose.
Question 18:

What temperature range best represents the ‘danger zone’ and increased risk of contracting food poisoning?

  • a. −30°C to −10°C
  • b. 30°C to 10°C
  • c. 5°C to 60°C
  • d. 40°C to 70°C
Question 19:

A prokaryotic cell can be distinguished from a eukaryotic cell by the:

  • a. Presence of a cell membrane
  • b. Absence of membrane-bound organelles
  • c. Presence of a nucleus
  • d. Presence of a cell wall
Question 20:

Autotrophs can be distinguished from heterotrophs by:

  • a. Their ability to carry out photosynthesis
  • b. The presence of chloroplasts in their cells
  • c. The ability to make organic molecules from simple inorganic ones
  • d. Their ability to carry out the process of fermentation
